_comment: HAND-COMPUTED expectations for probes/widgets/media/Main.as. Never regenerate these by running the probe.

_derivation.root: column, align-items flex-start, padding 20, gap 10, size [320,260]. Root rect (0,0,320,260); content starts at (20,20).
_derivation.img1: First child, explicit size [80,40] -> (20,20,80,40). An 8x8 solid #22AA55 source with scaleMode 'stretch': the whole 80x40 is the source colour.
_derivation.img2: Second child, y = 20 + 40 + 10 = 70, size [80,40] -> (20,70,80,40). scaleMode 'none' keeps the 8x8 source at 1:1, centred: x = 20 + (80-8)/2 = 56, y = 70 + (40-8)/2 = 86 -> the source covers (56,86)-(63,93).
_derivation.sv: Third child, y = 70 + 40 + 10 = 120, size [280,60] -> (20,120,280,60). The window is therefore rows 120..179.
_derivation.img3: Fourth child, y = 120 + 60 + 10 = 190, size [80,40] -> (20,190,80,40). scaleMode is LEFT OUT, so the default 'fit' applies: min(80/8, 40/8) = 5, i.e. a 40x40 bitmap centred in the node -- x = 20 + (80-40)/2 = 40, y = 190 + (40-40)/2 = 190 -> the source covers (40,190)-(79,229).
_derivation.bands: Three children of the viewport, each 280x40 with an explicit height, laid out in the viewport's default column: b1 (20,120,280,40), b2 (20,160,280,40), b3 (20,200,280,40). These are the LAYOUT rects and they do NOT move when the view scrolls -- scrollRect slides pixels, not the solve. Content height = 120 > 60, so maxOffsetY = 60.

points.img1_stretched: Anywhere inside img1's rect is the source colour. (60,40) is its centre = #22AA55.
points.img2_source: The centred 8x8 source of img2 spans (56,86)-(63,93), so its centre (60,90) = #22AA55.
points.img2_padding: (30,75) is inside img2's rect but outside the 1:1 source (which starts at x=56), so it shows the root background #FFFFFF. This is the pixel that proves 'none' really does not scale.
points.sv_band1: offset 0: rows 120..159 are b1 = #EE1111. Sample (160,140), clear of the viewport's edges.
points.sv_band2: rows 160..179 are b2's first 20 rows = #11EE11. Sample (160,170).
points.gap_above: The 10px gap between img2 (ends y=110) and the viewport (starts y=120) is #FFFFFF; sampled at (160,115).
points.img3_fit_fill: The fitted 40x40 bitmap of img3 covers (40,190)-(79,229), so its centre (60,210) is the source colour.
points.img3_fit_letterbox: (30,210) is inside img3's node but LEFT of the fitted bitmap (which starts at x=40), so it is the root background #FFFFFF. This is the pixel that proves the default really is 'fit' (contain) and not 'stretch'.

_derivation.behaviour: Steady-state layout solves do not increase after the settle capture. Then, in the program: contentH/maxOffsetY are 120/60 (a viewport that shrank its content would report 60/0); one wheel notch through Stage.dispatchWheel slides exactly wheelStep = 24px; the band that slid above the window does NOT paint over the gap above it (the clip); an over-large offset clamps to 60; and swapping img1's scaleMode to 'none' re-arranges the bitmap.
